question: In flowering plants, the fusion of the male and female gametes within the ovule is called ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**fertilisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fertilisation** is defined as the biological process of the fusion of **male gametes** (pollen) with **female gametes** (ovum/egg) to form a **diploid zygote**.
 
• In **Angiosperms** (flowering plants), this process occurs inside the **ovule**, which is located within the **ovary** of the **carpel** (the female reproductive organ).
 
• The process begins when a **pollen grain** germinates on the **stigma** and grows a **pollen tube** down the **style** to reach the **micropyle** of the **ovule**.
 
• Flowering plants undergo a unique process known as **Double Fertilisation**, which was first discovered by **S.G. Nawaschin** in the **year 1898**.
 
• In **Double Fertilisation**, one male gamete fuses with the **egg cell** to form the **zygote** (Syngamy), while the second male gamete fuses with **two polar nuclei** to form the **triploid (3n) Primary Endosperm Nucleus (PEN)**. *Hence, the statement regarding fusion within the ovule describes fertilisation, and option C is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pollination**:

 
 
• It is the **physical transfer** of pollen grains from the **anther** of a stamen to the **stigma** of a pistil.
 
• It is a **pre-fertilisation** event. It can be **Self-pollination** (within the same flower or plant) or **Cross-pollination** (between different plants).
 
• Common agents of pollination include **wind (Anemophily)**, **water (Hydrophily)**, and **insects (Entomophily)**.
 
 
 
• **Transpiration**:
 
 
• This is the **evaporative loss of water** from the aerial parts of the plant, primarily through the **stomata** on the **leaves**.
 
• It creates a **transpiration pull** which helps in the **ascent of sap** (upward movement of water and minerals) from **roots** to **leaves**.
 
• Factors affecting the rate include **temperature**, **light intensity**, **humidity**, and **wind speed**.
 
 
 
• **Germination**:
 
 
• This is the process by which an **organism grows from a seed** or similar structure.
 
• The **dormant embryo** becomes metabolically active and breaks through the **seed coat** to form a **seedling**.
 
• Essential conditions for this process include **water (imbibition)**, **oxygen** for respiration, and an **optimum temperature** (usually between **25°C to 30°C** for most plants).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Post-Fertilisation Changes**:

 
 
• After **fertilisation** occurs, the **zygote** develops into the **embryo**.
 
• The **ovule** matures and hardens its integuments to become the **seed**.
 
• The **ovary** grows rapidly and ripens to become the **fruit**, while the ovary wall becomes the **pericarp**.
 
• Other parts of the flower, such as **sepals, petals, and stamens**, usually wither and fall off.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Endosperm**:
 
 
• The **Endosperm** formed during **Triple Fusion** serves as a highly **nutritious tissue** that provides food to the developing **embryo** during its early stages.
